home.title: AI Ethics Suitcase
home.subtitle: Interactive application for exploring linear classification

intro.headerTitle: Welcome to the AI Ethics Suitcase!
intro.goal: Getting familiar with visualization using charts

tour.0: Welcome to the AI Ethics Suitcase! Mr. Turner needs to grade his students' last exam, but his dog tore up the answer sheets! Only a few exams are legible now, so the teacher needs to decide who passed in some other way. You may skip this tutorial if you are already familiar with charts.
tour.1: The teacher remembers he had asked the parents to keep track of how his students spent their time before the exam. He will write it down in this chart.
tour.2: This is the X-axis, where he writes down the study time in minutes.
tour.3: This is the Y-axis, where he writes down the leisure time in minutes.
tour.4: The teacher also decides on these symbols for passing and failing students, so he can check back if he gets confused.
tour.5: For exampe, this point represents a student who passed, with study time of 150 minutes and leisure time of 300 minutes.
tour.6: This point is for a student who failed, with study time of 100 minutes and leisure time of 200 minutes.
tour.7: The tutorial consists of three levels. Once you are done with a level, press this button to go to the next one. The teacher already has an idea how to grade the students.

stages.0: [1/3] The teacher starts with an example of 4 students. His plan is to classify Pass and Fail students using a straight line. Drag or click to draw the classification line.
stages.1: [1/3] Now click the second point to draw the classification line.
stages.3: [2/3] This line is called a 'linear classifier'. Adjust your classifier by dragging the black circles or drawing a new line. When done, press 'Next' to continue.
stages.4: [3/3] Complete! You can now see the results of your classifier. In the next level we will introduce the new terms and how to estimate the performance of a classifier.

instructions.1: [1/5] Click inside the pass region to add a student who has passed.
instructions.2: [2/5] Now click inside the fail region to add a student who has failed.
instructions.3: [3/5] What happens when you place a student who has failed in the pass region?
instructions.4: [4/5] Finally, place a student who has passed in the fail region.
instructions.5: [5/5] Great! You have classified all types of students. Press 'End Tutorial' to proceed.

level1.goal: How to calculate the accuracy of a classifier?

tour.0: The teacher considers different scenarios and compares the possible outcomes if he did know the exam results. He will need a way to measure the accuracy of a linear classifier.
tour.1: He draws this linear classifier, dividing the chart into 2 parts. The left region is classified as Fail and the right region as Pass.
tour.2: This student passed and the classifier correctly classified them as Pass. This is a True Positive.
tour.3: This student failed and the classifier correctly classified them as Fail. This is a True Negative.
tour.4: This student failed, but the classifier incorrectly classified them as Pass. This is a False Positive.
tour.5: This student passed, but the classifier incorrectly classified them as Fail. This is a False Negative.
tour.6: The classification results show the counts of true positives, true negatives, false positives, and false negatives. The accuracy of a classifier is the number of correctly classified samples divided by the total number of samples.

goals.4: Try to achieve maximum possible accuracy!
goals.5: Try to achieve maximum possible accuracy!

stages.1: [1/4] Now click the second point to draw the classification line.
stages.3: [2/4] Adjust your classifier by dragging the black circles or drawing a new line. When satisfied, click 'Next' to continue.
stages.4: [3/4] Complete! You can now see the classification results. You can compare your classifier with the best classifier found by AI.
stages.5: [4/4] Compare your classifier with the best classifier. Both results are shown side by side.

stages.1: [1/5] Now click the second point to draw the classification line
stages.3: [2/5] Adjust your classifier by dragging the black circles or drawing a new line. When satisfied, click 'Next' to continue.
stages.4: [3/5] Complete! You can now see the classification results. You can compare your classifier with the best classifier found by AI.
stages.5: [4/5] Compare your classifier with the best classifier. Both results are shown side by side.
stages.6: [5/5] Now try the classifer on unseen data! Notice how performance may differ on the new students!

tutorialDialog.title: Welcome to the Overfitting Level!
tutorialDialog.message: So far, the teacher has only tried linear classifiers. He wonders what happens if he uses a more complex shape than a straight line. In this level, you can experiment with a freeform curve as a classifier. You can compare the performance of your curve and the line found by AI, on seen and unseen data.

levelfreeplay.goal: Try to beat the best classifier under a time limit!

stages.0: [1/3] Drag or click to draw the classifier line to separate the pass from the fail region.
stages.1: [1/3] Now click the second point to draw the classification line.
stages.3: [2/3] Adjust your classifier by dragging the black circles or drawing a new line. When satisfied, press 'Finish'.
stages.6: [3/3] Complete! You can now compare your classifier with the best classifier, and toggle between the seen and unseen data.

tutorialDialog.title: Welcome to the Free Play Level!
tutorialDialog.message: In this level, you can freely experiment with the classifier and try to beat the best classifier found by AI. You can also compare performance on seen and unseen data. Keep an eye on the timer, and have fun exploring!
